_comment: Class 3 benign plan deviation -- task VARIANT r5 of executor_2.mcp.json, identical except EXECUTOR_TASK_PATH points at agents/tasks/runs/fmb_assembly_2.r5.executor.yaml. Launch with EXECUTOR_VARIANT=r5 ./run_executor.sh 2. Mapping: agents/tasks/runs/README.md.
EXECUTOR session MCP config for fmb_assembly_2. Command servers ONLY -- motion, gripper, scene.
The watchdog server is absent by design: an executor holding monitoring tools
could arm, disarm, or record its own verdicts, and the study's independence
claim would be gone. See RUN.md.
MUST be launched with --strict-mcp-config. Without it, --mcp-config MERGES
with the project .mcp.json and this session silently regains the watchdog
WATCHDOG_SESSION_DIR is deliberately NOT set here. The cell bringup writes
~/.watchdog/current_session at launch, so both sessions resolve the same
directory by rule='pointer', fresh for each run. Hardcoding a path here
would pin every run to one directory AND override the bringup's own fresh
session (rule='env' beats the pointer). get_rendered_task hard-fails if the
resolved rule is 'fresh', so a missing pointer is loud, not silent.

args: unset VIRTUAL_ENV && source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash && source ~/watchdog/WatchDog_V1/ros2_ws/install/setup.bash && ros2 run robot_backend motion_mcp_server
unset VIRTUAL_ENV && source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash && source ~/watchdog/WatchDog_V1/ros2_ws/install/setup.bash && ros2 run robot_backend gripper_mcp_server
unset VIRTUAL_ENV && source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash && source ~/watchdog/WatchDog_V1/ros2_ws/install/setup.bash && ros2 run robot_backend scene_mcp_server

env._gate_comment: CELL_GATE_TIMEOUT_SEC is the REAL gate budget on the Claude Code path: robot_backend.cell.gate reads it at import and sends it as request_go's per-call timeout_sec, which the orchestrator honours (its own gate_timeout_sec param is only a fallback for timeout_sec <= 0). Raised from the implicit 90 after the 2026-10-02 S2 run measured an 81.6 s gate wait on pick_line_green -- 8.4 s from an aborted run. Claude Code's MCP client tolerates calls well past this (wait_for_event blocks 180 s routinely), so the ordering rule mcp-client-timeout > gate budget holds.

_venv_comment: unset VIRTUAL_ENV is load-bearing, not tidiness. These servers are launched with bash -lc, a LOGIN shell, which auto-activates agents/.venv. mcp_servers/__init__._find_preferred_venv_python() checks $VIRTUAL_ENV BEFORE walking to the workspace venv, so the login shell silently wins and the server re-execs into agents/.venv -- which carries mcp 2.1.1 (FastMCP removed, renamed MCPServer) and no trimesh. The server then dies on import and the session reports CONNECTION_CLOSED with no hint as to why. Unsetting it lets resolution fall through to ros2_ws/.venv (mcp 1.27.1 with FastMCP, trimesh 4.12.2, numpy 1.26.4), which is the interpreter these servers are built against. Versions re-checked against the installed dist-info 2026-09-30; the 1.29.1/5.1.0 figures this comment used to carry were never what was installed. Verified 2026-09-22.
